analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-poison is caused by returning/using IR nodes that reference pool-allocated memory after that memory has been poisoned, due to unsafe constant-fold comparison on vector constructors. In Constructor::getVecComponent, iteration over `this->arguments()` (SkTArray) assumes the constructor/prefix argument tree is always valid and live; during constant folding (`IRGenerator::constantFoldVector` -> `PrefixExpression::compareConstant` -> `Constructor::compareConstant`), it descends through prefix/constructor operands and reads vector components from stale/invalid argument storage, triggering ASan in SkTArray::begin().
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via SkRuntimeEffect shader source that produces a negated vector-constructor constant comparison during binary-expression constant folding (PoC: `float n(){-2 .L1==- -2 .L1;}`). Data flow: fuzzer input -> `SkRuntimeEffect::Make` -> compiler IR generation -> `IRGenerator::convertBinaryExpression` -> `constantFoldVector` -> constant comparison between prefix-negated constructor expressions. The malformed numeric syntax leads to an invalid/stale constructor argument state, and `Constructor::getVecComponent` iterates `arguments()` without guarding against lifetime/validity, causing read from poisoned pool memory.
